renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: masked_share
  title: Masked share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of the assembly masked as repeat, with the lowest and the highest assembly next to it. It answers how repeat-rich the assemblies are.
    How to read: compare an assembly with its close relatives. A share far below them suggests a library that missed repeats, and a share far above a de novo library that over-called. RepeatMasker publishes no expected share.
    Source: https://www.repeatmasker.org/
  column: masked_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 100.0
  caption: median share of the assembly, with the range

- component: card
  id: interspersed_share
  title: Interspersed repeat share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of the assembly covered by interspersed repeats (transposable elements), with the spread across assemblies in the box. It answers how much of the masking is mobile elements rather than simple sequence.
    How to read: the gap between this and the masked share is simple repeats and low complexity sequence. A wide box means assemblies of very different repeat content.
  column: interspersed_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with the spread

- component: advanced_viz
  id: masked_vs_length
  title: Masked share against assembly length
  description: |-
    Each point is an assembly: its total length (horizontal) against the percentage of it that is masked (vertical), sized by the number of masked bases and coloured by its GC content. It answers whether repeat load grows with genome size.
    How to read: assemblies far above the trend are repeat-rich for their size, and assemblies far below it may have a library that missed repeats. RepeatMasker defines no cut-off here, so judge each point against related genomes.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median masked share of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of RepeatMasker.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    color_col: gc_pct
    x_title: Assembly length (bp)
    y_title: Masked share of the assembly (%)
    log_x: true
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: total_length
    y: masked_pct
    label: genome
    size: masked_bp

- component: table
  title: Masking summary per assembly
  description: |-
    Each row is an assembly: its sequences, length, GC, masked bases and the share masked by each repeat type. It answers how the repeat content breaks down per assembly.
    How to read: sort by the unclassified share to find assemblies whose library could not name the repeats.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: class_composition
  title: Repeat class composition
  description: |-
    Each bar is an assembly and each segment a repeat class, sized by the percentage of the assembly it occupies. It answers which kinds of repeat make up the masked part of each genome.
    How to read: the bar height is the total masked share, so tall bars are repeat-rich assemblies. A large unclassified segment means the library could not name those repeats. Switch the rank to open the families inside each class, and compare assemblies by the segments that differ.
    Source: https://www.repeatmasker.org/
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    default_rank: Class
    normalise_to_one: false
    top_n: 12
  roles:
    sample_id: genome
    taxon: repeat_class
    rank: rank
    abundance: genome_pct

- component: card
  id: repeat_elements
  title: Repeat elements masked
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of repeat elements masked across the classes, and the bar splits them by class. It answers which classes contribute the most copies.
    How to read: classes with many short copies, such as simple repeats, dominate the count even when they cover little sequence. Use the composition bar for the share of the assembly instead.
  column: elements
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: repeat_class
  filter_expr: col('rank') == 'Class'
  caption: elements, by class

- component: interactive
  title: Repeat class
  description: |-
    Choose one or more repeat classes or families to restrict the tiles of this tab to them. It answers how a single kind of repeat behaves across assemblies.
    How to read: pick a class such as a DNA transposon family to compare its share between assemblies.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: repeat_class

- component: table
  title: Repeat classes per assembly
  description: |-
    Each row is a class, family or summary line of one assembly: its element count, the bases it occupies and its share of the assembly. It answers exactly how much of an assembly each repeat type covers.
    How to read: filter the rank to Class so the rows partition the masked bases without double counting the families.
